topics.topic: Define marked_at event timing, clock authority, read behavior, and datetime representation
questions: Which exact event does `marked_at` denote: receipt of the mark request, completion of validation, acquisition of the project lock, or the instant immediately before the mark record is written?
From what authority does the deliverer obtain the instant written to `marked_at`?
What datetime representation must `marked_at` use, including timezone awareness and UTC normalization?
How many times may a mark operation read the decided time source, at which step is it read, and must replayed or conflicting mark calls read it at all?

Which clock supplies marked_at, when is it read relative to conflict checking and the durable write, how many readings does one mark operation take, and is the stored datetime naive UTC, offset-aware UTC or another representation?

quotes:
1. The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

2. Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

3. The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form. It sets `marked_at`.
judgement.why: P7 judged the same clock authority, event timing, read behavior and datetime representation, and the relevant passages have not changed.

topics.topic: Define the source_id format, validation pattern, type, and comparison normalization
questions: What is the exact value and type of `SOURCE_ID_PATTERN`, and therefore which strings are valid source ids?
Which textual representation of SHA-256 is source_id, and is the comparison with the imported SOURCE_ID_PATTERN-matching request exact or normalized?

quotes: | `SOURCE_ID_PATTERN` | `str` | `[0-9a-f]{64}` |

A `source_id` that does not match the imported `SOURCE_ID_PATTERN` constant in full is refused with
   `invalid_source_id`.
| 3 | the hash of the bytes differs from `source_id` | `SOURCE_CHANGED` |
judgement.why: The imported constant is a string pattern accepting exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters in full, so uppercase is refused and every accepted source id is compared directly with the hash without a case-normalization choice.

topics.topic: Define camera metadata field selection and fallback conditions for PreparedPhoto.taken_at
questions: Which camera metadata field or ordered set of fields is the camera record, and which missing, malformed, impossible or conflicting values cause fallback to the file modification time?

quotes:
3. The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.
judgement.why: P8 already judged the same camera-field precedence and fallback conditions, and the deciding passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Camera timestamp field precedence, validity, fallback, and UTC conversion for taken_at
quotes:
3. The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.

4. The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset, as the Client Portal stores it. A camera
   time with no offset is read in the configured time zone. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
precedent.why: A2 specifies the ordered camera fields, offset source, invalidity and plausibility rules, fallback, local-time edge cases and UTC conversion.

topics.topic: Define the assertions required to prove no work occurs before a valid confirmed connection
questions: What must the Required tests assert to show that nothing is scanned, placed or marked before a valid confirmed connection is established, rather than only checking the refusal answer and durable writes?

quotes: - INV-10: scan, placement and mark each answer `connection_not_confirmed` for an unconfirmed connection (`test_an_unconfirmed_connection_delivers_nothing`). After a scan has succeeded on the running service, clearing the confirmation makes scan, placement and mark each answer `connection_not_confirmed` and write nothing (`test_a_cleared_confirmation_stops_the_running_service`). For a valid file with no record for the project, scan, placement and mark each answer `unknown_project` and write nothing (`test_a_project_without_a_connection_delivers_nothing`). For an absent file, a file that cannot be opened, a file that is not UTF-8 or JSON, a file of another form and a record that breaks the form of rule 8, also when that record is unconfirmed or belongs to another project, scan, placement and mark each answer `folder_unavailable` and write nothing (`test_unreadable_connections_deliver_nothing`), and the service does not start (`test_the_service_does_not_start_with_an_unreadable_connection_record`). A scan, placement or mark that reaches its connection check reads the file exactly once (`test_each_operation_reads_the_connection_record_once`), a request refused earlier reads it zero times (`test_a_request_refused_before_the_connection_check_does_not_read_the_file`), and a file replaced after the reading does not change the running operation (`test_an_operation_finishes_on_the_reading_it_made`). A connection leaving its root is not loaded (`test_a_connection_cannot_leave_the_object_root`), and a linked folder outside the root is refused (`test_a_photo_folder_linked_out_of_the_root_is_refused`).
judgement.why: The Required tests passage is unchanged from the closed State 2 text, and the source-id-pattern change neither touched it nor made its test-observation question newly material.

topics.topic: Define when, where, how precisely, and how often file modification time is read
questions: At what step and from which object is the modification-time instant read, in which precision, and how many times may one placement operation read it?

quotes:
3. One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`. The service keeps no memory of earlier scans: it judges the name and the file when the call
   runs. The named file is read once, and the bytes that were read are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.

4. A file's modification time is converted to the same form before it is compared or delivered, dropping
   any fraction finer than a microsecond toward the earlier instant.
judgement.why: P6 already judged the same modification-time timing, consistency and precision question, and the deciding passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Timing and consistency of file modification-time reads
quotes:
3. One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`. The service keeps no memory of earlier scans: it judges the name and the file when the call
   runs. The named file is read once, and the bytes that were read are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.

4. A file's modification time is converted to the same form before it is compared or delivered, dropping
   any fraction finer than a microsecond toward the earlier instant.
precedent.why: Delivery does not reuse a scan observation: it judges and reads the file once when the delivery call runs, and that delivery-time modification instant is converted to the specified representation.
